candidates.summary: a []byte MsgCall argument now arrives with cap(b) = base64 DecodedLen(len(arg)) instead of len(b), so cap depends on padding and whitespace in the encoding
candidates.failure_scenario: MsgCall to `func Cap(cur realm, b []byte) int { return cap(b) }` with arg "AQ==" (one byte) returns 3; with "AQ==" followed by 400 newlines it returns 303. At the merge base both return 1. NewSliceFromData sets Maxcap = cap(data) and exposes data[:cap] as the base array, while base64.DecodeString returns dbuf[:n] over a DecodedLen-sized buffer. One argument value now reaches the realm as many distinct slices (the malleability the file header forbids), and a realm that stores b persists the slack bytes in its base array, sized by the sender's padding.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm -run TestFinder1SliceArgCapCall -v (tests/solo-finder-1-slice-arg-cap.go) at a5370a166 and at 6c49f5420; fix is alloc.NewSliceFromData(bz[:len(bz):len(bz)])
candidates.evidence: head: `arg len 4 -> cap(b) = (3 int)`, `arg len 404 -> cap(b) = (303 int)`; merge base: `(1 int)` for both. Direct convertArgToGno probe at head: `Length=1 Maxcap=3003 baseData=3003` for "AQ=="+4000 newlines.

candidates.summary: map-literal duplicate-key detection skips only non-comparable typed nils, so two typed nil pointer keys, which Go does not treat as constants, are rejected as duplicates; the ComputeMapKey keying makes map[any] reject what the merge base accepted
candidates.failure_scenario: `a := map[any]int{(*int)(nil): 1, (*int)(nil): 2}` compiles and prints len 1 under Go 1.25 and passes at the merge base, but at head preprocess panics `duplicate key (nil *int) in map literal`, so a package carrying it fails addpkg. The guard added this round (isComparable) covers slice/map/func and misses *PointerType, which is comparable but also folds to a non-constant ConstExpr. Sibling `map[*int]int{nil: 1, nil: 2}` fails at both head and base (pre-existing member of the same class).
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-1-nil-pointer-map-key.gno gnovm/tests/files/zz_finder1_nk1.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run 'TestFiles/zz_finder1_nk1' -count=1 at a5370a166 (FAIL) and 6c49f5420 (ok); fix: only hash keys whose kind is bool, string or numeric (a real Go constant)
